argumentation_roles.why_draw: make the nested Q1→Q2→Q3 decision pipeline and optimizer stages auditable
argumentation_roles.new_problem_use_conditions: use when there are multiple linked decision layers or a complex metaheuristic pipeline

argumentation_roles.why_draw: show graph-family structural differences before optimization
argumentation_roles.cannot_prove: optimizer scalability or why one method is best
argumentation_roles.new_problem_use_conditions: use only when structural covariates plausibly explain optimizer behavior

argumentation_roles.why_draw: show when peak live memory occurs and whether peaks flatten under schedule
argumentation_roles.supports_claim: temporal shape and reported Cmax for a given schedule
argumentation_roles.cannot_prove: global optimality or improvement without baseline trajectory on same graph
argumentation_roles.new_problem_use_conditions: use whenever peak-over-time is the actual objective; bind peak marker to Result Registry

argumentation_roles.why_draw: explain overlap, occupancy duration and spill timing by cache type
argumentation_roles.cannot_prove: optimality, scalability, or causal correspondence to operator semantics without trace linkage
argumentation_roles.new_problem_use_conditions: use for representative graphs; for very large graphs prefer zoomed windows plus summary statistics

argumentation_roles.figure_type: actual Pareto front / feasibility tradeoff plot
argumentation_roles.paper_gap: paper uses a generic Pareto schematic (Fig 6.14) and before/after radar (Fig 6.15), not an actual nondominated front
argumentation_roles.why_draw: show feasible nondominated solutions, hard transfer cap, chosen operating point and diversity
argumentation_roles.new_problem_use_conditions: required when claiming Pareto/DPEA/NSGA-II results; radar chart is not a substitute

style_observations: academic blue/teal algorithm boxes and table accents
cache Gantt plots use many categorical colors and become visually dense
body is formula-heavy; figures mainly serve structure and trajectory evidence rather than decorative illustration
figure_decision_lesson: For algorithmic scheduling papers, the minimum evidence set should be: graph/workload structure summary, matched baseline-vs-optimizer objective trajectory or result table, feasibility replay, runtime/quality budget comparison, and for multi-objective Q3 an actual feasible Pareto plot rather than only radar before/after.
